title: Configuration
text:
biblint.toml answers three questions:
Keep the file in version control, usually at the repository root. The command line chooses the operation (check or format); the configuration chooses the policy shared by both commands.

title: Configuration
text:
Find the right files
Without --config, biblint searches upward from the first input path until it finds biblint.toml. An explicitly supplied config path takes precedence. This means a command launched from a subdirectory still uses the repository policy.
For a directory input, biblint visits .bib files recursively. include and exclude patterns then decide which files are used:
include = ["**/*.bib"]
exclude = ["vendor/**", "generated/**"]
default-exclude = true
An explicit file does not need a .bib extension, although it is still subject to the configured include and exclude patterns. Recursive scans skip .git/** and target/** when default-exclude is true.

title: Configuration
text:
Select rules
The default rule set is a useful starting point. Use extend-select to add opt-in rules while keeping the defaults, or use select when you want to define the complete set yourself. ignore always wins over either selection method.
[lint]
# Add checks without removing the defaults.
extend-select = ["duplicate_doi", "key_format"]

# Replace the defaults entirely when a small, explicit set is preferable.
# select = ["syntax_error", "duplicate_key"]

# Disable a selected rule, including one added above.
# ignore = ["key_format"]
Use all as a wildcard. Per-file ignores use the same rule names and are useful for generated or legacy data:
[lint.per-file-ignores]
"generated/**" = ["formatting", "unsupported_construct"]
Formatting is not part of check by default because it is a rewrite rather than a content diagnostic. Use biblint check --format for a one-off formatting check, select formatting in the config, or use biblint format --check when formatting is the only gate you need.

title: Configuration
text:
A practical starter file
This profile scans project bibliographies, ignores vendored/generated files, adds duplicate DOI/citation and citekey checks, and sorts the output predictably:
include = ["**/*.bib"]
exclude = ["vendor/**", "generated/**"]
default-exclude = true

[lint]
extend-select = ["duplicate_doi", "duplicate_citation", "key_format"]

[lint.key-format]
style = "better-bibtex"

[format]
indent = 2
align = false
lowercase = true
sort = ["key"]
sort-fields = ["title", "author", "year"]
The key-format section enables the Better BibTeX-compatible style for checking existing keys. It does not rename them; see Citekey generation when you want to generate and apply new keys.

title: Configuration
text:
Validate a configuration
Unknown settings, rule names, invalid globs, and invalid citekey formulas are rejected when the configuration loads. Settings omitted from the file use their defaults, so start small and add only the policy your project needs.

title: Formatting
text:
biblint format writes a canonical representation of the BibTeX it understands. It is deliberately conservative: the default profile changes presentation, not the spelling of bibliographic values or the identity of entries.
Use --diff to preview a change, --check to make formatting a CI gate, and no flag to write the configured profile:
The command above prints a unified diff and leaves references.bib untouched. Once the diff is acceptable, run biblint format references.bib to write it.

title: Formatting
text:
Default shape
Input:
@ARTICLE{Smith2024,
author={Smith, John},
title={A Study},
year=2024
}
Default output:
@article{Smith2024,
  author = {Smith, John},
  title = {A Study},
  year = 2024
}
The default profile lowercases entry types and field names, uses two-space indentation, and separates entries with a blank line. It does not align equals signs, sort entries or fields, add braces, change values, or remove duplicate and empty fields.

title: Formatting
text:
Layout and ordering
Set layout preferences under [format]:
[format]
indent = 2                 # a space count, or "tab"
align = false              # or a field-name column number
blank-lines = true
lowercase = true
trailing-commas = true
wrap = 80                  # false disables wrapping
sort = ["key"]             # true uses key order
sort-fields = ["title", "author", "year"]
sort controls entry order. sort-fields controls field order within each entry; true uses biblint’s built-in field order. Lists provide an explicit order, and fields not named in a list remain after the named fields.

title: Formatting
text:
Value transforms
These options change value spelling or representation, so enable them only when that is part of the repository’s policy:







Setting
Effect




curly
Enclose values in braces.


numeric
Render numeric values as bare literals.


months
Normalize recognized month names.


format-page-ranges
Normalize page ranges.


escape / unescape
Convert supported text between Unicode and LaTeX.


encode-urls
Encode URL underscores.


strip-enclosing-braces
Remove one outer brace group.


enclosing-braces / remove-braces
Select fields whose brace depth changes.


drop-all-caps
Convert all-caps values to title case.


wrap
Wrap long values at a configured width.


lowercase
Lowercase entry types and field names; enabled by default.



The escape table is package-independent. Characters that have no built-in LaTeX escape are preserved and reported by unsupported_escape when the relevant check is enabled.

title: Formatting
text:
Cleanup and semantic transforms
Use these settings when you intentionally want to remove, merge, or otherwise change data:
[format]
remove-empty-fields = true
remove-duplicate-fields = true
omit = ["abstract"]
strip-comments = true
tidy-comments = true
max-authors = 3
generate-keys = true
duplicate-kinds = ["doi", "citation"]
merge = "combine"
merge accepts first, last, combine, and overwrite. When duplicate-kinds is empty, merging considers DOI, citation, and abstract duplicates. Add key if key duplicates should also be merged. Without a merge strategy, duplicate entries are preserved.
generate-keys uses the same formula evaluator as the key_format rule. See Citekey generation for the supported Better BibTeX syntax.

title: Formatting
text:
Fix safety
check --format --fix applies the formatting diagnostic only when formatting is enabled, and it applies safe fixes by default. Add --unsafe-fixes when the configured profile includes a transform that can remove information or change entry identity:
biblint check references.bib --format --fix --unsafe-fixes
This safety gate covers citekey generation, merging, omission or removal of fields/braces/comments, all-caps conversion, unescaping, duplicate/empty-field cleanup, and author truncation. The standalone format command applies the configured profile directly, so preview it with --diff first.

title: Formatting
text:
Preserved source
Comments, special entries, and unstructured source are retained unless a configured transform targets them. Unstructured source is reported as unsupported_construct rather than discarded.

title: Citekey generation
text:
biblint can check existing citation keys and generate deterministic suggestions from BibTeX entries. There are two separate choices:








Goal
Setting
Result




Audit existing keys
key_format under [lint]
Reports a suggestion; never renames a key.


Apply generated keys
generate-keys under [format]
Replaces keys while formatting.



The better-bibtex style implements a deterministic subset of Better BibTeX’s formula syntax and reads only data present in the .bib file. Unsupported functions and filters are rejected when the configuration loads.


The built-in formula is:
auth.lower + year + shorttitle(1,0)
It:

uses the first creator surname, falling back through author, editor, translator, and collaborator
lowercases that surname
appends the first four digits found in year
appends the first significant word of title

shorttitle removes common stopwords before counting words. The 0 preserves the title fragment’s original capitalization.
For example, this entry:
@article{old,
  author = {Smith, John},
  title = {A Study of Things},
  year = {2024}
}
produces the suggestion smith2024Study. Existing keys reserve their values, so collisions receive alphabetic suffixes such as a, b, and aa. Entries without enough key material are left unchanged.



Keep the formula in the repository’s biblint.toml:
[lint]
extend-select = ["key_format"]

[lint.key-format]
style = "better-bibtex"

[format]
generate-keys = true

[format.key-generation]
formula = "auth.lower + year + shorttitle(1,0)"
collision-suffix = "alphabetic"
The formula in this example is the default and can be omitted. With only key_format enabled, check reports differences but does not rename existing keys. generate-keys = true enables replacement as a formatter transform.
To inspect key suggestions without writing files:
biblint check references.bib
To preview the generated keys and any other configured formatting changes:
biblint format references.bib --diff
The standalone format command applies the configured profile directly after you review the diff. If you apply the profile through check --format --fix, key generation is an unsafe fix and must be explicit:
biblint check references.bib --format --fix --unsafe-fixes



When generated keys change, biblint can update references in one related Markdown, Quarto, or R Markdown document. Pass an explicit .md, .qmd, or .Rmd path while checking exactly one explicit BibTeX file:
biblint check references.bib --format --fix --unsafe-fixes --update-markdown manuscript.qmd
The option requires --format, --fix, and --unsafe-fixes because citation key changes affect document identity. It updates Pandoc-style bracketed citations, including citations with multiple keys or locators, and textual citations.
Fenced code, inline code, HTML tags, HTML comments, and email-like addresses are preserved. A directory check or standard-input check cannot use this paired update.
For author/year keys that reserve the first suffix letter, use collision-suffix = "skip-a". This formula uses the full surname for one creator and the first three letters of up to three creators otherwise:
[format.key-generation]
formula = "auth(0,m=2) ? auth(3,m=1) + auth(3,m=2) + auth(3,m=3) + shortyear : auth + shortyear"
collision-suffix = "skip-a"
Creator lists follow standard BibTeX name syntax: separate creators with the word and.



Formula names are case-insensitive. The evaluator supports:

direct BibTeX fields, such as title, doi, and shortauthor
quoted strings and numbers, for example "-" and 2024
concatenation with +
fallbacks with ||, and top-level alternate patterns separated by a semicolon or |
conditional composition with &&
ternaries such as language == "en" ? "eng" : ""
length comparisons using ==, !=, <, <=, >, or >=
chained filters such as auth.lower.clean
positional and named function arguments, such as substring(start=1,n=3)

The implemented entry functions are:

creators: auth, authAuthEa, authEtAl, authEtal2, authForeIni, authIni, authorIni, authorLast, authors, authorsAlpha, authorsn, and authshort
entry fields and metadata: date, extra, firstpage, journal, language, lastpage, month, origdate, origyear, shortyear, title, type, and year
title fragments: shorttitle and veryshorttitle

The implemented filters are abbr, alphanum, ascii, capitalize, clean, condense, default, discard, len, lower, nopunct, nopunctordash, numeric, postfix, prefix, replace, select, skipwords, substring, transliterate, and upper.
For example, this formula uses a short author field from Better BibTeX’s extra data when it is present and otherwise falls back to the BibTeX author:
extra('tex.shortauthor').clean.lower || auth.lower
extra(...) reads matching key: value lines from the BibTeX extra field. Functions and filters outside the supported lists are configuration errors.



The same BibTeX input and committed configuration produce the same suggestions. Existing keys are reserved, and collision suffixes are assigned in document order. Because a generated key can be referenced outside the .bib file, preview key changes and update related citations in the same reviewed change.

title: biblint
text: biblint checks BibTeX files for syntax and bibliography problems, then formats them into a consistent representation. Keep the configuration in your repository so local runs and CI use the same policy.

title: biblint
text:
A safe first workflow

1. Check the project
Run the linter from the project root. A directory is searched recursively for .bib files, and the default-enabled rules run automatically unless your configuration selects a different set.
biblint check .


2. Preview formatting
Use --diff when you want to inspect the formatter’s exact changes. This command does not write files.
biblint format . --diff


3. Apply the profile
After reviewing the diff, format the project in place:
biblint format .
If you want biblint to make only safe changes while checking, use check --format --fix. Content-changing transforms remain disabled unless you explicitly add --unsafe-fixes.

title: biblint
text:
Pick the command by goal








I want to…
Use
What happens




Find syntax and lint issues
biblint check .
Reports diagnostics; writes nothing.


Include formatting in the check
biblint check . --format
Adds a formatting diagnostic; writes nothing.


Fix safe issues automatically
biblint check . --format --fix
Writes safe fixes, including formatting.


Format files directly
biblint format .
Writes the configured representation.


Gate formatting in CI
biblint format . --check
Reports files that would change and exits nonzero.


Review a formatting diff
biblint format . --diff
Prints a unified diff and writes nothing.


Integrate diagnostics with a tool
biblint check . --output json
Prints diagnostics as JSON.


Learn about a rule
biblint rule <name>
Prints that rule’s summary and fix status.

title: biblint
text:
What biblint reads

A directory contributes .bib files recursively.
An explicit file is checked even if its extension is not .bib.
- reads one BibTeX document from standard input.
biblint.toml is discovered by searching upward from the first input path.

See Configuration for include/exclude patterns and rule selection. See Formatting for the changes made by default and the transforms you can opt into.






WarningBefore enabling transforms



Formatting is intentionally conservative by default. Options such as citekey generation, merging, field removal, brace removal, and author truncation can change content or citation identity. Preview them with biblint format <path> --diff before writing, and use --unsafe-fixes when applying them through check --format --fix.

title: biblint
text:
Continue with a task

Configure a project — choose files, rules, and formatting policy
Format BibTeX — understand defaults and opt-in transforms
Explore rules — enable checks, suppress individual entries, and find duplicates
Generate citekeys — use the supported Better BibTeX formula subset
Develop biblint — run workspace checks and render this site

title: Rules
text: Rules report problems in a BibTeX project. Run biblint check to use the configured rule set, biblint rule to list every rule, or biblint rule <name> to read one rule’s summary and fix status.

title: Rules
text:
Rule reference
The default set focuses on syntax and structural problems. Formatting, citekey style, and project-wide duplicate comparisons are opt-in:










Rule
Default
Severity
Fix
Purpose




syntax_error
yes
error
none
BibTeX syntax is incomplete or unbalanced.


formatting
no
note
safe
The file would be reformatted by biblint.


missing_key
yes
warning
none
An entry has no citation key.


key_format
no
warning
none
An existing key differs from the configured key formula.


duplicate_key
yes
warning
none
A citation key is used more than once.


duplicate_doi
no
warning
none
Two entries share a DOI.


duplicate_citation
no
warning
none
Two entries share a normalized citation fingerprint.


duplicate_abstract
no
warning
none
Two entries share an abstract fingerprint.


duplicate_field
yes
warning
none
An entry repeats a field name.


empty_field
yes
warning
none
A field has no value.


nonstandard_name_separator
yes
warning
none
A creator list uses with or a comma before and.


invalid_suppression
yes
warning
none
A suppression comment is malformed, misplaced, or obsolete.


unsupported_escape
yes
note
none
A character has no built-in LaTeX escape.


unsupported_construct
yes
note
none
Source was preserved because it could not be structured.



Warnings produce exit status 1; errors produce exit status 2. Notes are still diagnostics and therefore also make check return 1 when they are reported. See Configuration for changing the selection.

title: Rules
text:
Inline suppressions
Place a standalone % biblint-ignore comment immediately before the entry it belongs to. Name one or more rules, and optionally add a reason after ::
% biblint-ignore nonstandard_name_separator duplicate_field: legacy source
@book{garfinkel1997,
  author = {Simson Garfinkel with Gene Spafford},
}
The directive applies only to the next BibTeX entry. Multiple directives before one entry are combined. Suppressions cannot hide syntax errors or whole-file formatting diagnostics, and malformed, misplaced, or unused directives are reported by invalid_suppression.
nonstandard_name_separator checks author, editor, translator, and collaborator values. It only examines text outside nested braces and does not rewrite values. A literal phrase such as Smith with Jones can be protected by bracing the intended literal name.

title: Rules
text:
Select rules
Use select to replace the default set, extend-select to add to it, and ignore to disable a rule regardless of how it was selected:
[lint]
select = ["duplicate_key"]
extend-select = ["key_format", "duplicate_doi"]
ignore = ["unsupported_escape"]
Use all as a wildcard. Per-file exceptions use the same rule names:
[lint.per-file-ignores]
"generated/**" = ["formatting", "unsupported_construct"]
Formatting is not enabled for check by default because it is a mechanical rewrite rather than a content diagnostic. For a one-off formatting check, add --format to the command. For a formatting-only gate, use biblint format <path> --check.

title: Rules
text:
Project-level checks
When checking a directory or multiple files, biblint also detects duplicates across files. DOI, citation, and abstract comparisons are disabled by default; enable only the comparisons useful for the project. A single explicit file gets single-file checks and does not create a project-wide comparison.

title: Rules
text:
Key-format checks
key_format is disabled by default because changing a citation key can break references elsewhere. Enable it explicitly to report suggestions:
[lint]
extend-select = ["key_format"]

[lint.key-format]
style = "better-bibtex"
The rule reports a suggestion but does not rename keys automatically. See Citekey generation to configure the formula and, if desired, apply generated keys through the formatter.

title: Development
text:
biblint is a Rust 2024 workspace with four crates:
The minimum supported Rust version is 1.88. Keep parser, formatter, and rule changes lossless: source biblint cannot structure must remain visible rather than being dropped.

title: Development
text:
Before submitting a change
Run these checks from the repository root. Each command answers a different question, so a failure is easier to diagnose when they are run separately.
First, check that Rust formatting is unchanged:
cargo fmt --all -- --check
Then run Clippy with warnings treated as errors:
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
Finally, run the full workspace test suite:
cargo test --workspace

title: Development
text:
Adding behavior
Keep formatting policy in biblint-format, configuration and diagnostics in biblint-core, and CLI concerns in biblint. Add focused regression tests for new transforms and rules.
The citekey formula evaluator follows the same boundary: its syntax is inspired by Better BibTeX, but its implementation and tests live in biblint and operate on BibTeX data only. Do not add a Zotero-only construct unless there is a deterministic BibTeX representation for its inputs.

title: Development
text:
Render the documentation
The website source is in docs/ and is rendered with Quarto. Render it after editing the .qmd or Markdown sources:
quarto render docs
For an interactive local preview that refreshes as you edit:
quarto preview docs
Generated output lives in docs/_site/ and is ignored by Git.
